s1.syndrome_frame: Acute to subacute onset of painful, itchy, and bleeding skin lesions with a mixture of pustules and plaques, primarily affecting the face, scalp, trunk, and extremities, with a significant impact on mobility
salient_findings: Pustules and hemorrhagic-crusted plaques on the scalp, legs, arms, and trunk
Keloidal plaques on the face
Difficulty walking due to skin lesions
Epidermal hyperplasia and exocytosis of neutrophils on histopathology
Dense dermal-mixed inflammatory cell infiltration with microabscesses
key_facts: Teenaged male patient
2-week history of skin lesions
Lesions began as pustules and developed into painful, itchy plaques
Prior treatment with prednisolone, clindamycin hydrochloride, and fluconazole
Continued development of new lesions despite treatment
Difficulty walking due to skin lesions
Pustules and hemorrhagic-crusted plaques on the scalp, legs, arms, and trunk
Keloidal plaques on the face
Negative HIV test result
Histopathology showing epidermal hyperplasia, exocytosis of neutrophils, and dense dermal-mixed inflammatory cell infiltration
Microabscesses scattered with eosinophils on histopathology
No granulomas or multinucleated giant cells on histopathology
Negative periodic acid-Schiff staining

shortlist.label: Pyoderma gangrenosum
shortlist.why_kept: Painful, itchy, and bleeding skin lesions with pustules and plaques, consistent with clinical presentation

shortlist.label: Sweet syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Acute onset of painful, itchy, and bleeding skin lesions with a mixture of pustules and plaques, matching the syndrome frame

shortlist.label: Erythema elevatum diutinum
shortlist.why_kept: Pustules and plaques on the extremities, with a significant impact on mobility, aligning with the case context

shortlist.label: Generalized pustular psoriasis
shortlist.why_kept: Pustular skin lesions with a subacute onset, consistent with the patient's symptoms and histopathology findings

shortlist.label: Acute febrile neutrophilic dermatosis
shortlist.why_kept: Neutrophilic dermatosis with fever, consistent with the patient's symptoms and laboratory results

raw.rationale: The patient's symptoms, including painful and itchy plaques, pustules, and histopathology showing epidermal hyperplasia, exocytosis of neutrophils, and dense dermal-mixed inflammatory cell infiltration, are consistent with Sweet syndrome. The presence of microabscesses scattered with eosinophils and the negative periodic acid-Schiff staining also support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Pyoderma gangrenosum
rejected.why: While pyoderma gangrenosum can present with painful ulcers, the histopathology in this case does not show the characteristic necrotic ulcers and undermining borders typically seen in pyoderma gangrenosum.

rejected.label: Erythema elevatum diutinum
rejected.why: Erythema elevatum diutinum is characterized by purple-red plaques and nodules, which are not described in this case. The histopathology also does not show the characteristic fibrinoid necrosis and leukocytoclastic vasculitis seen in erythema elevatum diutinum.

rejected.label: Generalized pustular psoriasis
rejected.why: While generalized pustular psoriasis can present with widespread pustules, the histopathology in this case does not show the characteristic parakeratosis and Munro's microabscesses seen in psoriasis.

rejected.label: Acute febrile neutrophilic dermatosis
rejected.why: Acute febrile neutrophilic dermatosis is a synonym for Sweet syndrome, so it is not a distinct diagnosis to reject.
